sourceNote: Original Evia practice questions mapped to course criteria. These are not official awarding-body or end-point-assessment questions.

questions.prompt: What should a worker do with site induction and safety-sign information?
options: Understand and follow it throughout the work
Ignore it after the first day
questions.explanation: Induction information and safety notices remain part of the site's control arrangements.

questions.prompt: An uncontrolled hazard presents serious and immediate danger. What is the correct action?
options: Stop work, move to safety and report it through the site procedure
Take a photograph and carry on
questions.explanation: Work should stop when serious danger is not controlled, and the issue must be reported.

questions.prompt: What should be considered before moving a heavy masonry component?
options: Load, individual capability, task, environment and suitable assistance
questions.explanation: A handling assessment considers the task, load, person and environment, with aids or help used where needed.

questions.prompt: On hearing the evacuation alarm, what should you do?
options: Follow the site emergency procedure and go to the designated assembly point
questions.explanation: The site emergency plan gives the safe route, assembly point and reporting process.

questions.prompt: What should influence the selected method of work?
options: Project information, resources, conditions and the risk assessment
questions.explanation: A suitable method must meet technical requirements while controlling risks and using available resources.

questions.prompt: The project information is insufficient to choose a safe method. What should happen?
options: Obtain the necessary information from an authorised source
questions.explanation: Missing information must be obtained before the method is confirmed.

questions.prompt: What makes a useful personal work sequence?
options: A list based only on preference
An order based on the work, resources, dependencies and site programme
questions.explanation: Sequencing should reflect resources, interfaces and the required programme.

questions.prompt: A delay will affect the agreed programme. What should you do?
options: Identify the effect and inform the relevant person promptly
questions.explanation: Early reporting allows the programme and interfaces to be managed.

questions.prompt: Which choice best supports low-carbon working?
options: Planning quantities and methods to reduce waste and unnecessary plant use
Sending reusable materials to mixed waste
questions.explanation: Efficient resources and methods can reduce waste, transport and energy demand.

questions.prompt: Which behaviour supports equality and diversity at work?
options: Withholding information from a new starter
Communicating respectfully and adapting so relevant people can participate
Ignoring a request for reasonable support
questions.explanation: Respectful, inclusive communication helps people contribute safely and effectively.

questions.prompt: Your work will affect another occupation's access. What should you do?
options: Clarify and coordinate the activities with the people involved
questions.explanation: Interfaces should be agreed so work can proceed safely and efficiently.

questions.prompt: Which method can help set out a right angle on site?
options: A 3-4-5 triangle checked to suitable dimensions
Following the nearest wall without checking
questions.explanation: A correctly measured 3-4-5 triangle is a practical right-angle check.

questions.prompt: What should control a drainage run's line, level and fall?
options: The approved drainage design and specified datum
questions.explanation: The design establishes where the system runs and how it drains.

questions.prompt: Before entering or working beside a drainage trench, what must be confirmed?
options: Only that the pipe has arrived
The excavation controls, access and ground conditions are safe
That spoil is at the edge
questions.explanation: Excavation collapse, access, services and plant movement require effective controls.

questions.prompt: Why is correctly prepared bedding important below a drainage pipe?
options: It provides continuous support and helps maintain line and fall
questions.explanation: Uniform support reduces point loading and keeps the pipe at its designed alignment.

questions.prompt: How should pipe sockets, seals and lubricant be assembled?
questions.explanation: Correct seals, cleanliness, lubricant and insertion method are needed for a sound joint.

questions.prompt: Why should open drainage pipe ends be capped during installation?
options: To prevent debris entering and obstructing or damaging the system
questions.explanation: Temporary caps keep soil, mortar and other debris out of the system.

questions.prompt: Why is an insertion-depth mark useful on a push-fit drainage joint?
options: It shows whether the pipe has been inserted to the required position
questions.explanation: A clear witness mark helps verify correct joint assembly.

questions.prompt: Where should rodding or inspection access be provided?
options: At the locations required by the design so the system can be inspected and cleared
questions.explanation: Designed access points allow maintenance at changes and other required locations.

questions.prompt: What is most important during initial backfill around a pipe?
options: Tip large rubble directly onto it
Use the specified material and placement method without disturbing line, fall or joints
Compact with any plant on the pipe
questions.explanation: Correct surround and controlled placement protect the pipe and preserve its alignment.

questions.prompt: When should a new drainage run be tested and checked?
options: At the specified stage before concealment or backfill prevents inspection
questions.explanation: Testing while the work is accessible allows faults to be located and corrected.

questions.prompt: A drainage test fails. What should happen next?
options: Keep the work accessible, identify and rectify the cause, then retest
questions.explanation: A failed system must be investigated, corrected and shown to comply before it is covered.

questions.prompt: How should foul and surface-water connections be identified?
options: From the approved drainage information and verified connection points
questions.explanation: Misconnections can cause pollution or flooding, so destinations must be confirmed from approved information.

questions.prompt: What should a drainage quantity take-off include?
options: Pipe lengths, fittings, access components, bedding or surround and a justified allowance
A fixed percentage unrelated to the design
questions.explanation: The take-off must reflect all designed components and an appropriate, justified allowance.
